payload.analysis: Based on current market conditions and inflation expectations, allocating 10% of the portfolio to gold can provide a suitable inflation hedge. Gold has historically maintained a strong positive correlation with inflation, as it tends to increase in value when inflation rises. This is largely due to gold's function as a store of value, which is often at odds with paper currencies during periods of inflation when those currencies tend to depreciate. In our analysis, we find that gold's inflation correlation coefficient is particularly strong during times of high inflation, implying that it would be a useful addition to the portfolio during such periods. We also note that the current allocation to gold falls below the rebalancing trigger threshold, suggesting that some re-allocation might be warranted.
